document.title: Meadows Housekeeping Work Queue Implementation Plan
document.headline: Build the operational workflow in small, independently testable stages

workCoverage.coverageDescription: Defines a twelve-stage development and testing plan for extending the existing Meadows Housekeeping intake and normalized-record viewer into a complete Work Queue and Recommendations Queue workflow. The plan covers queue-sheet schemas, intake routing controls, duplicate-safe queue writers, persistent sorting state, queue viewers, task status transitions, JSON note history, active and completed filtering, completion email idempotency, completed-work history, later archiving, a final end-to-end test, and a strict stage-by-stage implementation order.

primaryProject.projectGoal: Transform normalized intake records into traceable working records that can be sorted, started, annotated, completed, reported, reviewed historically, and later archived without changing the source record.
primaryProject.projectPhase: pre-implementation architecture and staged test planning
primaryProject.contributionType: workflow design, schema definition, implementation sequencing, test planning, and risk control
primaryProject.identificationBasis: The document explicitly presents a Work Queue and Recommendation Queue implementation plan with twelve development stages.

relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: The existing intake viewer displays normalized source records and will receive routing buttons and persistent sorted-state labels.
relatedProjects.impact: The viewer becomes the entry point for creating Work Queue and Recommendations Queue records.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The plan explicitly begins from the current intake log viewer.

relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: Recommendations receive their own linked records, statuses, notes, viewer, and archive behavior without using task-completion email logic.
relatedProjects.impact: Suggestions and recommendations can be reviewed separately from operational work.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The plan defines a separate Recommendations Queue schema and viewer.

relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: Completion email is sent only after the working record is successfully completed and is protected by a persistent sent flag.
relatedProjects.impact: The system can notify the original requester exactly once while preserving retry capability after delivery failure.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The completion email sequence and tests are explicitly specified.

sharedFoundations.name: Normalized source records
sharedFoundations.relationshipDescription: Every working or recommendation record retains a Source ID pointing to the original normalized request.
sharedFoundations.impact: Source history remains unchanged while operational state evolves separately.

sharedFoundations.name: Derived working records
sharedFoundations.relationshipDescription: Queue sheets hold status, timestamps, notes, and email state associated with a source record.
sharedFoundations.impact: Operational changes can occur without rewriting intake history.

sharedFoundations.name: Visible staged testing
sharedFoundations.relationshipDescription: Each stage must produce a visible, reliable result before the next feature is added.
sharedFoundations.impact: Prevents routing, status, notes, email, and archive failures from being debugged simultaneously.

projectContext.relationshipSummary: The plan connects the existing normalized intake viewer to two derived queue systems, then extends the Work Queue through status, notes, completion, email, history, and archive stages while preserving source-record integrity.

subject.mainFocus: Designing a staged, testable path from normalized intake records to persistent Work Queue and Recommendations Queue workflows.
subject.description: Implementation plan for queue schemas, routing, viewers, state changes, JSON notes, completion handling, notifications, history, and archiving.

narrative.promptingSituation: The current system could capture and normalize source records and display them in an intake viewer, but it did not yet provide a complete operational lifecycle for sorting, working, annotating, completing, notifying, and retaining records.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The queue should not mutate the original source record. A separate working record must carry operational state while remaining linked by Source ID.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create a dependable workflow from supervisor submission through queue assignment, task execution, notes, completion, email notification, completed history, and later archive.
narrative.approach: Divide the system into twelve stages, define the data model and allowed transitions, specify visible browser behavior, provide test cases for each stage, and require successful verification before proceeding.

progression.title: Define queue storage
progression.description: Add Work Queue and Recommendations Queue tabs with consistent columns for source linkage, status, timestamps, notes, and email state.
progression.result: The operational data layer is specified before interface behavior is added.

progression.title: Add intake routing controls
progression.description: Place Work Queue and Recommendations Queue buttons on unsorted cards and first verify only that the correct Source ID is emitted.
progression.result: Browser interactions can be tested without risking sheet changes.

progression.title: Create duplicate-safe queue writers
progression.description: Append linked working records while rejecting duplicate or cross-queue sorting.
progression.result: A source record can enter one intended workflow exactly once.

progression.title: Persist sorting state
progression.description: Combine source records with queue Source ID lists so handled cards remain visibly sorted after refresh.
progression.result: The intake viewer reflects durable server state rather than temporary browser state.

progression.title: Build dedicated queue viewers
progression.description: Join working records to their original normalized source content and render Work Queue and Recommendations cards.
progression.result: Operational users can work from derived records without losing source context.

progression.title: Add mutable task behavior
progression.description: Introduce validated status transitions and append-only JSON notes with timestamps.
progression.result: Tasks gain a controlled operational history.

progression.title: Separate active and completed work
progression.description: Filter completed tasks out of the active viewer while retaining both source and working records.
progression.result: Active work remains focused while completed history persists.

progression.title: Add exactly-once completion notification
progression.description: Send email only after successful completion and persist a Completion Email Sent flag for duplicate prevention and safe retry.
progression.result: Completion communication becomes reliable and idempotent.

progression.title: Add completed history and later archiving
progression.description: Display duration, notes, and email state for completed tasks, then later move records into an archive view by status rather than deletion.
progression.result: The full lifecycle remains queryable without destroying records.

progression.title: Prove the whole system
progression.description: Run a complete request through submission, normalization, routing, work, notes, completion, email, refresh, and source-integrity checks.
progression.result: The architecture is accepted only when all state survives refresh and the source remains unchanged.

problemsEncountered.problem: Multiple interdependent workflow systems could be built and debugged at the same time.
problemsEncountered.effect: Failures in routing, state, notes, email, and archive behavior would become difficult to isolate.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Use a strict staged implementation in which each visible result is proven before the next function is added.

problemsEncountered.problem: The same source could be placed in both queues or duplicated.
problemsEncountered.effect: One request could generate conflicting or repeated working records.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Check both queue tabs before append and return an already-sorted failure result when necessary.

problemsEncountered.problem: Completion actions and email sending could be repeated.
problemsEncountered.effect: Timestamps could be overwritten and requesters could receive duplicate completion messages.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Write timestamps only when blank, reject invalid transitions, and use Completion Email Sent as an idempotency flag.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Implement the entire queue lifecycle in one development pass.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: The components form one obvious end-to-end workflow.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: The plan explicitly rejects debugging queue, status, notes, email, and archive systems simultaneously.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Complex operational workflows should be decomposed into independently visible and testable increments.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Delete or move completed and archived records.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: Removing inactive records could appear to simplify active views.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: The design requires history, notes, timestamps, source linkage, and later archive retrieval to remain intact.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Lifecycle views should be filters over persistent records, not destructive movement.

turningPoints.title: The queue became a linked working layer
turningPoints.description: Source ID was established as the bridge between immutable normalized submissions and mutable operational records.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The system became a joined-record architecture rather than a single row changing purpose.

turningPoints.title: Visible testing became part of the architecture
turningPoints.description: Each stage received explicit success, failure, persistence, and edge-case tests.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Verification became a development gate rather than a final afterthought.

turningPoints.title: Completion email was made idempotent
turningPoints.description: The sequence stores completion before sending and separately marks successful delivery.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The notification system gained retry safety and duplicate prevention.

keyDecisions.reason: The source must remain the permanent evidence of what was submitted.
alternativesConsidered: Store task state directly on the source row
consequences: Every queue record requires Source ID linkage.
Viewers must join source and working data.

keyDecisions.decision: Prevent one Source ID from entering both queues.
keyDecisions.reason: A request should not accidentally create conflicting operational interpretations.
alternativesConsidered: Allow duplicate queue records and reconcile later
consequences: Queue-writing functions must check both destination sheets before append.

keyDecisions.decision: Use JSON arrays for note history.
keyDecisions.reason: Multiple timestamped notes must remain in one working record without losing earlier entries.
alternativesConsidered: Create a new sheet row per note
consequences: The script must parse, validate, append, serialize, and safely handle malformed JSON.

keyDecisions.decision: Filter completed and archived work rather than delete it.
keyDecisions.reason: History, source linkage, timestamps, and notes must remain available.
consequences: Viewer behavior depends on status filters.
The working record remains the lifecycle history.

keyDecisions.decision: Add archiving only after the active lifecycle is reliable.
keyDecisions.reason: Archiving adds another state and view before core work behavior is proven.
alternativesConsidered: Build archive behavior alongside initial queues
consequences: Archive is explicitly deferred to stage 12.

narrative.methodEstablished: Build one visible behavior at a time, preserve source records, store mutable workflow state in linked records, verify persistence after refresh, reject duplicates and invalid transitions, and add communication only after state is safely committed.
narrative.result: The document establishes a complete implementation blueprint and acceptance-test structure for the Work Queue and Recommendations Queue lifecycle.
lessonsLearned: Derived workflow records need explicit source lineage.
Browser state is not enough; sorting must be persisted and reconstructed from stored records.
Duplicate prevention must check all mutually exclusive destinations.
Status transitions should be explicit and irreversible by default.
Structured note history requires defensive JSON handling.
Completed and archived views should filter persistent records rather than move or delete them.
Email should occur after successful state persistence.
A sent flag is necessary for exactly-once communication and safe retry.
Complex systems are easier to verify when every stage produces visible evidence.
narrative.directionChange: The project moved from a conceptual intake-and-routing idea to a precise staged implementation plan with schemas, transitions, tests, and final acceptance criteria.
narrative.narrativeSummary: The plan defines how normalized submissions become durable Work Queue or Recommendations records, how those records evolve through status and notes, and how completion, notification, history, and archive behavior will be built and proven incrementally.

supervisor.plainLanguageSummary: The plan explains how requests will move from the current intake viewer into separate Work and Recommendations queues, then through notes, status changes, completion, notification, and history.
supervisor.operationalImpact: Each request will remain tied to its original submission while staff work from a separate record that can safely change over time.
supervisor.currentStatus: The workflow, record structures, implementation order, and test requirements are fully planned; the document does not claim the twelve stages are implemented.
risksOrLimitations: The plan requires disciplined stage-by-stage implementation.
Duplicate and cross-queue sorting must be blocked.
Malformed Notes JSON must not destroy existing history.
Completion emails must not be sent twice.

general.summary: A twelve-stage implementation and testing blueprint for building linked Work Queue and Recommendations workflows from normalized source records.

technical.summary: The plan defines queue schemas, browser Source ID commands, Apps Script queue writers, cross-queue duplicate validation, source joins, finite task-state transitions, defensive JSON-note updates, status-filtered views, and an idempotent completion-email sequence.
keyPoints: Source and working records remain separate
Sorting state is reconstructed after refresh
Started and Completed timestamps are write-once
Completion email uses a persistent sent flag

projectSpecificLessons: The current intake viewer can be extended safely by routing only Source IDs and preserving normalized source records.
Work Queue and Recommendations Queue need distinct schemas and lifecycle rules.
The Work Queue working row can serve as the durable lifecycle history rather than creating separate sheets for every state.
generalLessons: Design the data model before adding interface controls.
Mutually exclusive destinations require shared duplicate validation.
Persistent server state must drive labels after browser refresh.
Join failures should degrade locally rather than collapse an entire page.
Append-only note arrays preserve chronological work context.
State changes and notification delivery should be committed separately.
A retryable sent flag is safer than assuming email delivery succeeds.
Filtering is often preferable to moving or deleting records.
Incremental visible tests reduce compound debugging.

recurringProblems.problem: Several dependent workflow features are implemented before any one is verified.

recurringProblems.problem: Browser labels are treated as persistent state.
recurringProblems.pattern: A card appears sorted until refresh because queue membership was not read from storage.

recurringProblems.problem: External notification is coupled too tightly to state change.
recurringProblems.pattern: A failed or repeated email can corrupt completion behavior or produce duplicates.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Linked source and working record architecture
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Preserve immutable intake records while keeping status, notes, timestamps, and delivery state in a Source-ID-linked working record.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Cross-queue duplicate prevention
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Check all mutually exclusive destination stores before appending a routed record.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Write-once task lifecycle timestamps
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Set Started At and Completed At only when blank and reject backward transitions by default.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Defensive JSON note history
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Parse, validate, append, and serialize note arrays without losing existing data when malformed input is encountered.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Exactly-once completion email with retry
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Commit completion first, send afterward, and persist a sent flag only after successful delivery.

knowledgeBaseCandidates.title: Stage-gated implementation testing
knowledgeBaseCandidates.description: Require one visible reliable result before adding the next dependent subsystem.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Never change the normalized source record to represent operational state.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: Work Queue and Recommendations records remain linked derivatives.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not allow one Source ID to enter both routing destinations.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: Queue writers must validate across both queue tabs.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not overwrite existing Started At or Completed At values.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: Lifecycle timestamps are evidence and should be write-once.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not delete completed or archived records.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: Views should filter persistent lifecycle records by status.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not send completion email until the completed working record has been saved.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: State persistence must precede external communication.

rulesConfirmedOrRevised.rule: Do not add the next implementation stage until the current stage has visible test evidence.
rulesConfirmedOrRevised.explanation: This isolates defects and prevents compound debugging.

tests.name: Stage 1 — queue sheet structure
tests.notes: Verify headers, text Source IDs, timestamps, valid [] note text, and Apps Script tab lookup.

tests.name: Stage 2 — card routing controls
tests.notes: Verify two buttons per card, correct Source IDs, card isolation, mobile behavior, and no writes.

tests.name: Stage 3 — queue writes and duplicate rejection
tests.notes: Verify correct append, unchanged source, same-queue duplicate rejection, and cross-queue rejection.

tests.name: Stage 4 — persistent sorting state
tests.notes: Verify labels and hidden buttons survive refresh and duplicate attempts from multiple tabs are blocked.

tests.name: Stage 5 — Work Queue viewer
tests.notes: Verify one card per working row, correct source join, empty state, warning card, and refresh stability.

tests.name: Stage 6 — Recommendations viewer
tests.notes: Verify only recommendations appear, notes do not change source, malformed records are safe, and no completion email fires.

tests.name: Stage 7 — status transitions
tests.notes: Verify allowed transitions, direct completion, write-once timestamps, backward rejection, and source integrity.

tests.name: Stage 8 — JSON note history
tests.notes: Verify multiple notes, special characters, blank rejection, malformed JSON protection, order, and refresh persistence.

tests.name: Stage 9 — active/completed filtering
tests.notes: Verify completed work leaves active view, appears in Completed, and retains all records and timestamps.

tests.name: Stage 10 — completion email
tests.notes: Verify exactly one email, correct recipient and content, invalid-address safety, false flag on failure, retry, and recommendation exclusion.

tests.name: Stage 11 — completed-work history
tests.notes: Verify one completed card, no active tasks, safe missing timestamps, readable notes, visible email state, and persistence.

tests.name: Stage 12 — archive
tests.notes: Verify archive filtering, source retrieval, preserved notes and timestamps, and no deletion.

tests.name: Final end-to-end system test
tests.notes: Verify the entire twenty-one-step workflow and confirm the original source record was never changed.

email.subject: Work Queue and Recommendations Implementation Plan
email.body: The implementation plan defines a staged path from the current intake viewer to separate Work and Recommendations queues. Each queue record will remain linked to the original source request, while task status, notes, timestamps, completion history, and email state are stored separately. Every stage must pass visible tests before the next is added.
